verdict_reason: The two paper-defined families are exact. Li et al.'s collection-level Distinct-n is implemented correctly: ten duplicate [1,2] completions give 0.100000 (2 types / 20 tokens), against 1.000000 for the per-completion mean that is kept separately under `mean_distinct_n`. Self-BLEU's primary path literally calls Texygen's own kernel (nltk sentence_bleu, uniform 1/max_n weights, SmoothingFunction().method1) with Texygen's `get_bleu_parallel` aggregation (every OTHER sentence in the collection), and the NLTK-free fallback matches NLTK to 5.551e-17 over 300 random pairs, returning exactly 0.000000000 on the disjoint anchor [7,8,9,10] vs [[1,2,3,4]] and exactly 0.367879441 on the brevity anchor [1,2,3,4] vs [[1..8]]. The caveat is the BLME-only entropy add-on: entropy positions are still taken as the FIRST len(trimmed) score rows rather than by a raw-position validity mask, so for continuation [1,0,2,3,4] with a distinct pad id 0 the last-quarter mean reads 7.000000000 where the correct value at the surviving raw positions is log(5) = 1.609437912 (absolute error 5.390562088). It is latent whenever pad_token_id == eos_token_id (the EOS break path is correctly aligned), which covers the gpt2/pythia zoo.
comparable_reason: The tokenizer channel is much weaker than round 1 claimed and I RETRACT it as a blocker: retokenising the identical 36 gpt2 completions with the Pythia BPE moves mean_self_bleu 0.060759 -> 0.060578 (-0.30%) and distinct_1 0.476108 -> 0.478336 (+0.47%), so cross-BPE comparison is fine. What is NOT fine is sampling noise at the shipped budget of 6 prompts x 6 samples x 32 tokens (about 1,150 tokens) with NO seed pinned. Three independent runs of the shipped config on gpt2 gave distinct_1 0.486979/0.483507/0.459201 (rel range 5.83%), mean_self_bleu 0.049850/0.054223/0.058914 (16.68%), sampling_entropy_collapse_delta -0.457749/-0.377563/-0.630446 (51.76%) and mean_phrase_repetition_rate 0.000000/0.006705/0.006705 (150%). Against that, three models x three runs give between-model sd / within-model sd = 2.03 (distinct_1), 3.22 (mean_self_bleu), 1.98 (entropy delta), 2.99 (phrase repetition) -- i.e. a single unseeded run carries 10-20% of its variance as generation noise. Absolute values are also not Texygen's, because Texygen scores nltk word tokens: the same 36 texts give mean_self_bleu 0.041008 as words vs 0.060759 as gpt2 subwords (-32.51%).
github_reason: Fetched SelfBleu.py from master and read `calc_bleu` (nltk.translate.bleu_score.sentence_bleu with weight = (1/ngram,)*ngram and SmoothingFunction().method1) and `get_bleu_parallel` (`other = reference[:index] + reference[index+1:]`). BLME's `_self_bleu_single` makes the identical NLTK call and `evaluate` uses the identical all-other-sentences aggregation, so the primary path is Texygen by construction; its NLTK-free fallback reproduces NLTK to 5.551e-17 over 300 random pairs (299 of them nonzero). Two documented divergences: Texygen's SelfBleu defaults to gram=3 while BLME hardcodes max_n=4 (both are grams the Texygen paper reports), and Texygen tokenises with nltk.word_tokenize where BLME uses model subword ids (-32.51% on the same texts). Li et al. 2016 released no code for Distinct-n.
paper_reason: Neither source publishes a number this task could reproduce: Li et al. 2016 report distinct-1/distinct-2 for their own seq2seq/MMI models on OpenSubtitles and Twitter dialogue, and Zhu et al. 2018 report Self-BLEU-2..5 for GAN text generators on COCO Image Captions and EMNLP News. Both are model-, corpus- and decoding-specific and none involves a pretrained LM on these eight prompts. The definitional anchors DO reproduce exactly (Distinct-n 0.100000 on the ten-duplicate collection; NLTK Self-BLEU to 5.551e-17).
confounds_reason: The obvious channels test clean. Tokenizer: retokenising identical text across two BPEs moves mean_self_bleu -0.30% and distinct_1 +0.47%. Vocabulary ceiling: distinct_1's denominator is ~1,150 generated tokens against a 50,257 vocabulary, so there is no log(V) or V/N saturation. Sampling support: with the pinned top_k = 0, the processed scores are finite on ALL 50,257 entries, so the entropy family is not capped by a filter width. What I could NOT rule out is a size correlation -- only three models were affordable at this generation cost, and their ordering (distilgpt2 mean_self_bleu 0.147249, gpt2 0.064229, pythia-70m 0.063569) is consistent with either a capability effect or a parameter-count effect. Test on the full zoo before treating it as size-free.
